Voat does not prevent external links within custom CSS. A good example of this can be found here:

https://voat.co/v/scribble

The subverse's custom CSS contains these lines:

header-banner>a:after{content:" ";background:url(i.imgur.com/NK49svv.png)

background:url(mh1.co/scribble/alerts/1.4.3.png)

Which loads an image from imgur.com AND a 1x1 pixel 'image' from the mh1.co server. This is really putting users at risk by enabling tracking of IP addresses.

That other site does not permit external image hosts. How can Voat do the same?

I think it's a fair trade off. The only alternative would be to "host" them here with base64 or something similar. People who are honestly worried about this can turn off custom style sheets and they will be fine.

And limiting external sites means they need a higher character limit. I can't do /v/fatpeoplehate's css because of the limit and tons of subs will have a similar issue. Killing creativity with limiting the external sites and no increase of character limit.

How about a whitelist? Allow known hosts like imgur, veuer, etc; reject unknowns; have a clear application process.

No, this isn't perfect; but anyone seriously concerned about their anonymity should be using anonymizing software on their side, and the fringe benefits of allowing site elements to get their bandwidth from other sites can't be ignored. Voat doesn't have the same level of financial support as leddit.
